spots.n: Golden Gate Bridge → Sausalito bike & ferry loop
spots.s: THE San Francisco date: pedal 8 easy miles over the bridge, linger over waterfront drinks in Sausalito, then ferry back past Alcatraz at golden hour.
Cypress cliffs, shipwreck views and haunting bathhouse ruins on the city's wildest edge — the walk-and-talk first date that never misses.
Grand 1898 food hall where the Saturday Foodwise farmers market (8a–2p) is a grazing crawl of oysters, porchetta sandwiches and bay views.
Bernard Maybeck's swan-lagoon rotunda is the most romantic 30 minutes in the city — golden hour here is an unfair advantage.
The evening boat gets you a smaller crowd, cellhouse audio in the dark and the skyline lit up on the ride back — book weeks ahead.
Hang off the running board over Russian Hill, hop out at the crooked block — touristy, sure, and still one of the great cheap thrills in America.
The city's sunniest people-watching lawn — grab Bi-Rite ice cream, claim a slope, and watch all of San Francisco show up on a warm Saturday.
Strong American and global collections, and the free 9th-floor observation tower is a secret 360° view most tourists never find.
Drive up, layer up, and watch the fog river pour over the city at dusk — the classic end to a first date that went well.
Mile of sand with the bridge filling the whole northern sky — bring a jacket and stay for the light show at sunset.
Ferry out, loop the 5-mile Perimeter Road past immigration-station history, and picnic with 360° bay views — a full-day date in one ticket.
Pier 15's giant playground of perception experiments — go Thursday for After Dark (18+, cocktails) when it turns into the smartest bar in town.
Climb the garden stairways past hidden cottages and wild parrots, then take in the 1934 murals and the best close-up skyline panorama.
New parkland stitched over the highway tunnels — campfire circles, food trucks at the Transit Café, and dead-on Golden Gate views.
Rent a pedal boat, circle Strawberry Hill's waterfall island, split snacks at the boathouse — an easy, talky Golden Gate Park classic.
The oldest public Japanese garden in the U.S. — arched drum bridge, koi, and tea service that makes an unhurried conversation easy.
Seven floors of modern heavyweights plus the living wall — a rainy-day date you can stretch into hours without running out of things to say.
Free-entry warehouse of coin-op machines from the 1900s — bring quarters, challenge your date to century-old arm wrestling.
Garlic fries, kayaks waiting for splash hits in McCovey Cove, and the prettiest ballpark backdrop in baseball — great low-pressure hang.
An acoustic sculpture on a Marina jetty that plays the tide through concrete pipes — weird, free, and a guaranteed conversation piece.

nightlife.s: Fillmore boutique club where the room runs hip-hop, R&B and Afrobeats with real headliners passing through — dress up, book a table if flush.
Multi-room SoMa megaclub with an LED cathedral of a main floor — hip-hop nights downstairs in LVL 55 while EDM shakes the ceiling.
The 2024-born warehouse club that revived 11th Street — serious sound, dusk-to-dawn house and techno bookings, Friday and Saturday only.
Art-deco warehouse with a Funktion-One rig — disco, house and the occasional hip-hop takeover for people who actually dance.
Mission backyard institution — cheap drinks, oyster happy hours, and the legendary seasonal Salsa Sunday parties on the patio.
Big Mission salsa palace with live orchestras Friday and Saturday — full dance floor, dressed-up crowd, lessons early if you need them.
The country's first purpose-built jazz hall — world-class bookings in a room with no bad seat; a can't-miss impress-your-date ticket.
Dim Civic Center cocktail den with live jazz seven nights and no cover most of them — first-date insurance in bar form.
Password-at-the-door 1920s speakeasy with library rooms and serious whiskey — book the hidden Wilson & Wilson bar-within-the-bar.
The 1912 hall where Bill Graham built rock history — chandeliers, free apples at the door, and posters for the shows you'll brag about.
John Lee Hooker's old juke joint across from the Fillmore — sweaty funk, soul and boogaloo bands until 2a most weekends.
Downtown K-town-style private suites plus an open-mic main bar — the low-stakes group night that always ends louder than it started.
39th-floor Marriott lounge with fan-window views of the whole glittering city — arrive before sunset, order something brown and slow.
Three-deck rum shrine with 550+ bottles and waterfall decor — the menu is a world tour and the room does half the conversation.
All-night SoMa institution — Bootie mashup Saturdays, goth and hip-hop one-offs, and a 4a license when everything else closes.
Proper Hotel rooftop with fire pits above Market Street — blankets, hot cocktails, and skyline intimacy that photographs like a movie set.

eats.s: Kyoto-kaiseki-inflected omakase in FiDi from a Michelin-recognized counter — the polished special-occasion splurge that earns it.
Twelve seats, four guests per chef, Michelin star — the intimate NoPa counter where every piece comes with a story.
Edomae counter in SoMa that's held a Michelin star since 2016 — Toyosu fish, hushed room, bring someone worth impressing.
The decades-old wharf-adjacent favorite reborn at 430 Folsom with a dry-aging program and Michelin star — SF sushi's glow-up story.
Hayes Valley's hip-hop-soundtracked omakase — inventive nigiri, no dress code, and a price you pick; the fun end of the ladder.
Inner Sunset institution since 1981 — generous nigiri and a chatty counter, the every-month sushi habit rather than the splurge.
Tiny Noe Valley counter punching way above its size — pristine fish and clever sauced pieces without omakase pricing.
Japantown's line-out-the-door hakata tonkotsu — creamy 20-hour broth and firm thin noodles worth every minute of the wait.
Tokyo ramen master Tomoharu Shono's Tenderloin outpost — the toripaitan and A5 wagyu bowls that started SF's ramen arms race.
Chez Panisse-trained izakaya cooking over binchotan — handmade udon, perfect yakitori, and the prettiest courtyard room in the Mission.
Michelin-starred Thai in Japantown — Pim Techamuanvivit's curries and charred prawns make it the city's smartest group dinner.
The Clement Street original whose tea leaf salad, tossed tableside, has kept a line on the sidewalk for two decades.
Corey Lee's charcoal Korean BBQ — Michelin-starred galbi and banchan precision; book ahead, bring carnivores.
Japantown's cheese-capped braised short-rib phenomenon — messy, rich, and built for sharing across the table.

chinese.s: Chinatown's Sichuan standard-bearer — chili-oil wontons and mala chicken from a chef who cooked for presidents; order the explosive pepper dishes.

chinese.n: Chong Qing Xiao Mian 重庆小面
chinese.s: Z&Y alumni slinging Chongqing-style hand-pulled noodles in numbing red broth — the honest 火辣 lunch counter of Kearny Street.
Michelin-starred Cantonese in a grand old Chinatown banquet hall — Dutch crunch BBQ pork and Peking duck for two under lotus chandeliers.

chinese.n: Good Mong Kok Bakery 好旺角
chinese.s: Cash-friendly Stockton Street window where locals queue for har gow, siu mai and BBQ pork buns by the bagful — eat them in Portsmouth Square.
Richmond District's glam Cantonese — five-color soup dumplings and carts by day, all-you-can-eat hot pot by night.
Geary Boulevard dim sum destination the Chronicle keeps on its Top 100 — get the baked BBQ pork buns before 1p or they're gone.
Inner Sunset's cult Shandong house — the dry-fried chicken wings are a city-wide obsession; write your name on the whiteboard and wait.

chinese.n: Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory 金門餅食
chinese.s: Ross Alley's 1962 factory where cookies are still folded by hand off hot irons — 50 cents buys a warm flat one and a great story.

chinese.n: Chinese Historical Society of America 美国华人历史学会
chinese.s: The nation's oldest Chinese-American museum, reopened 2026 in Julia Morgan's landmark YWCA — the context that makes Chinatown click.

chinese.n: Chinese New Year Festival & Parade 舊金山新年大巡遊
chinese.s: America's biggest Lunar New Year parade — 288-foot golden dragon, firecrackers and a million spectators every late Feb–early Mar; 2026's Year of the Horse edition ran March 7.
Grant Avenue's since-1972 wok emporium — Tane Chan's staff will talk you into the right carbon-steel pan and season it with advice.
The Richmond's real eating street — dumplings, roast duck, HK bakeries and Green Apple Books in ten blocks; start at 6th Ave and graze.
Outer Sunset Xi'an specialist — biang biang noodles and cumin lamb burgers that taste like a Silk Road detour off the N-Judah.

chinese.n: Hang Ah Tea Room 杭雅茶室
chinese.s: Tucked in a Chinatown alley since 1920 — America's oldest dim sum house still steaming baskets in a room the size of a train car.
The polished cart-service classic by Rincon Center — Shanghai dumplings and crisp-skin peking duck; pricier, worth it for the ritual.
Since-1972 Hong Kong-style counter on Kearny — shrimp wonton noodle soup in under ten minutes for under fifteen bucks.

chinese.n: New May Wah Supermarket 新美華
chinese.s: Clement Street's workhorse Asian supermarket — Sichuan peppercorns, live fish tanks and every sauce your 川菜 project needs.
Grant Avenue tasting bar where the pourers keep your gaiwan full and the banter flowing — a sneaky-great low-key date stop.

chinese.n: Tin How Temple 天后古廟
chinese.s: The oldest Taoist temple in America (1852), three flights above Waverly Place — incense spirals, harbor goddess, donation entry, quiet awe.

fishing.s: Four generations of Rescinos run this classic wooden boat off Berth 3 — salmon's back for 2026 after the three-year closure, plus halibut, rockfish and crab combos.
Fisherman's Wharf six-pack-to-full-boat operation chasing bay halibut, stripers and ocean rockfish — CA license required aboard, easy walk-on trips.
The Bay Area's storied license-free salmon pier — when the fish run, the rail is elbow-to-elbow; Dungeness crab snares Nov–Jul the rest of the year.
Throw swimbaits into the trough at first light for striped bass all summer — bring a CA license (shore fishing isn't exempt) and respect the rip.
License-free pier at the foot of the Golden Gate — crab pots, jacksmelt and the occasional halibut with the bridge filling your backdrop.
Berkeley Marina's hard-fishing fleet leader — potluck bay trips stacking halibut, stripers and rockfish; license required, gear rentable.
East Bay landing with daily rockfish/lingcod runs to the Farallones and 2026 salmon dates when CDFW windows open — check the season calendar.
SF's own trout-stocked lake — pedal-boat calm, bass in the tules, and a CA license on your phone is all the paperwork.
Horseshoe Cove's license-free pier under the bridge's north tower — jacksmelt, perch and crab with Marin Headlands quiet.
State rec area piers on the bay's warm southeast shore — a striper and sturgeon spot in season, license-free from the piers.

biking.s: Fairfax's famous 9-mile purpose-built loop in the county where mountain biking was born — buy the $5 day pass (Boy Scout land) and earn every bench-cut turn.
The Bay Area's first purpose-built flow trail — 1.5 miles of berms and rollers off the Tamarancho loop; same day pass covers it.
Rare legal state-park singletrack — 12+ swoopy miles of oak-shaded Shoreline and Bay View trails above San Pablo Bay; beginner-friendly, never boring.
Climb the 1896 'Crookedest Railroad' bed from Mill Valley to East Peak — a steady 8-mile grade through the very hills where klunkers invented the sport.
A eucalyptus cloud forest hiding real singletrack in the dead center of the city — fog-slick roots, zero drive time.
SF's biggest dirt network — 7 miles of rideable trail plus the Philosopher's Way loop; scrappy, hilly, and empty on weekdays.
Honest label: mellow bridle paths and Polo Field laps, not singletrack — but it's the easiest spin-and-coffee ride in the city.
The paved standout: a 1.7-mile Headlands climb to the postcard bridge-over-fog shot — pairs perfectly with the Sausalito loop.

social.s: The world's longest-running free outdoor swing dance (since 1996) on JFK Drive — free beginner lesson at noon, strangers become partners by 12:15.
Mission midweek staple — bachata then salsa-on-2 lessons from 7:30, social dancing to 1:30a; rotation-friendly and beginner-kind.
Live salsa orchestras in a Jackson Square courtyard — dressed-up, dance-first crowd; take the early lesson and stay till close.
The famous MOM weekly — DJ Gordo Cabeza spinning Motown originals and remixes to a packed, friendly floor; $5 after 9p kills your Monday blues.
Thursdays the Academy goes 21+ — DJs under the whale, cocktails by the swamp, planetarium date add-on; the easiest mingling in town.
Free 6:27a Wednesday workout crew — hills, stairs and hugs from strangers who become your people; just show up once.
10k bootcamp run with a boombox — music, exercise stops and a pub finish; pace groups mean nobody gets dropped.
SF's biggest trivia operation runs weeknight quizzes at bars citywide (Spark Social, Patriot House and more) — teams of strangers welcome.

social.n: Chinatown Night Market 唐人街夜市
social.s: Voted the country's #1 night market — five blocks of Grant Avenue food stalls, lion dancers and games on Waverly, second Fridays in season.

social.n: SF Chinese–English Language Exchange 中英语言交流
social.s: Weekly Saturday Mandarin/English tables — half the room wants your English, you want their 中文; RSVP on Meetup for the week's venue.
Roller disco in a deconsecrated 1880s church — disco lights, rental skates, and a floor where laughing at yourself is the icebreaker.
Inner Sunset board game café with hundreds of titles and waffle sandwiches — $7 buys unlimited table time and easy conversation.
